trial_title: Feasibility Study of Transcutaneous Tibial Nerve Stimulation for Urinary Symptoms in People With Multiple Sclerosis
brief_summary: Neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction is common among people with Multiple sclerosis with a pooled prevalence of 68.41% using self-report measures and 63.95% using urodynamic studies. eligibility_table.criterion: Self-reported diagnosis of any type of Multiple Sclerosis
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of SLE with transverse myelitis, which is related to Multiple Sclerosis, but there is no self-reported diagnosis of MS.
criterion targets female; patient is male
The patient's conditions and history suggest significant mobility issues, particularly with a history of CVA and altered mental status.

eligibility_table.criterion: At least one bladder storage related symptom (e.g. urinary frequency, urinary urgency, nocturia with or without incontinence).
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a neurogenic bladder, which typically includes bladder storage symptoms.

eligibility_table.criterion: People with an indwelling urethral catheter or indwelling suprapubic catheter
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a suprapubic catheter, which is considered an indwelling catheter.
The patient has a history of Non-hodgkins Marginal Zone Lymphoma, which could be considered a urologic disease.
There is no indication of diabetes mellitus in the patient's profile.

eligibility_table.criterion: Pregnant women or planning to be pregnant during the study time
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is male and there is no indication of pregnancy.
The patient has had a colostomy, which is a pelvic-related surgery within the last year.

eligibility_table.criterion: Pacemaker or other metallic internal devices
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of significant medical interventions, but there is no mention of a pacemaker or metallic devices.

eligibility_table.criterion: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) during recruitment phase.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has recurrent UTIs, which disqualifies them during the recruitment phase.
